# ESPEN - Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases

> > WHO Africa's platform for coordinating and supporting the elimination of neglected tropical diseases through preventive chemotherapy and transmission control across the African region.

ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) is a WHO African Regional Office initiative that supports Ministries of Health across Africa in their efforts to control and eliminate preventable neglected tropical diseases including lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, onchocerciasis, soil-transmitted helminthiases, and trachoma through mass drug administration and integrated disease management strategies.

## Key Topics

- Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs)
- Preventive Chemotherapy (PC)
- Lymphatic Filariasis
- Schistosomiasis
- Mass Drug Administration (MDA)
- Disease Elimination Programs
- WHO African Regional Office (AFRO)
- Ministries of Health (MOH)
- NTD Control Strategies
- Regional Expert Advisory Groups
- Onchocerciasis
- Soil-Transmitted Helminthiases
- Trachoma
- Africa Health Initiatives
- WHO Eastern Mediterranean Regional Office (EMRO)
